Ornamental:  Widely planted as an ornamental and avenue tree.Rhamnus prinoides

Ornamental:  R. arboreum (Lali Guras in Nepal) is distributed throughout the length of Nepal at a variety of altitudes. It is known for its variably colored blossoms, which come in shades of red, pink and white. The blossoming plants are a spectacular sight, with up to twenty blossoms in a single truss.Rhus natalensis
Ornamental:  R. heudelotii is a popular avenue tree in Uganda.Robinia pseudoacacia
Ornamental:  A beautiful liane for shady gardens, flowers beautiful and fragrant.Salix babylonica
Ornamental: S. koetjape is planted for aesthetic purposes along avenues and in parks.Santalum album

Ornamental:  The species is quite attractive, especially when in flower, and suitable for home gardens and urban environments, in a mixture of host species, and high protection.  Perhaps the greatest value of growing sandalwood in the landscape is the satisfaction of nurturing this esteemed cultural tree.  The flowers and berries are attractive, and the flowers are mildly scented.Sapindus mukorossi
Ornamental:  The attractive trees are suitable for planting in amenity areas.Schefflera heptaphylla
Ornamental:  S. volkensii has a majestic form and can beautifully grace gardens and avenues.Schinus molle
Ornamental:  S. terebinthifolius has an attractive appearance and has therefore been introduced in many areas as an ornamental and street tree.Schizolobium parahybum
Ornamental: S. longipedunculata is a beautiful flowering tree with potential as an ornamental in parks and gardens.Senna atomaria
Ornamental: It is now popular as an ornamental plant owing to its bright yellow flowers and black-green bracts.  It is used as ornamental plant in Africa.Senna siamea
Ornamental:  S. singueana is quick growing and very ornamental, often being in full flower at the height of the dry season.Senna spectabilis
Ornamental:  S. grandiflora is widely planted for beautification because of its giant showy flowers and long pods.Sophora japonica

Ornamental:  S. campanulata has been planted as an ornamental throughout the tropics. The flowers bloom with great profusion, and the trees can be seen from great distances. It is not browsed by domestic animals and although a popular  decorative tree for avenues it has shallow roots and a tendency for branches to break off in a storm.Spondias purpurea
Ornamental:  This lovely tree often flowers and fruits when leafless. It makes a good garden plant because of its adaptability.Stereospermum kunthianum
Ornamental:  The physical attributes of S. henningsii, shiny foliage, pleasant shade and fragrant flowers make it a suitable choice for gardening.Swietenia humilis
Ornamental:  Planted as a lawn tree in peninsular Malaysia.Swietenia mahagoni
Ornamental:  This is a beautiful tree suitable for gardens.Syzygium cordatum
Ornamental:  S. cumini is one of the most popular avenue trees in India.Syzygium jambos
Ornamental: T. donnell-smithi is grown as an ornamental on account of its impressive yellow floral display.Tabebuia rosea
Ornamental:  The evergreen habit and the beautiful flowers make it suitable for ornamental planting in parks, along roads and riverbanks.Tamarix aphylla
Ornamental:  T. camphoratus is a popular indigenous ornamental in South Africa, specially suited for bonsai with its aggressive root system.Taxus baccata
Ornamental:  The species is valued as an amenity tree by virtue of its many yellow trumpet-shaped flowers.Tecomaria capensis

Ornamental:  T. grandis is occasionally cultivated in tropical countries as an ornamental for its large leaves and spreading flower clusters. The species was originally introduced into Malaysia as a roadside and ornamental tree.Telfairia pedata
Ornamental: T. candida is occasionally utilized as an ornamental.Tephrosia vogelii
Ornamental: This tree is often planted on roadsides and, and is also used for ornamentation.Terminalia bellirica
Ornamental:  T. brownii is suitable for planting in amenity areas.Terminalia catappa
Ornamental: Widely planted as a street and shade tree in Nairobi, Kenya, and as far as the coast.Thespesia populnea
Ornamental:  The attractive tree is suitable for planting in amenity areas.Tithonia diversifolia
Ornamental: A popular avenue tree planted along roadsides in north India.Toona sureni
Ornamental: It is often planted as a garden tree. Its fast growth makes it a popular choice for a new garden.Trichilia emetica
Ornamental: The spreading multiple branches and small yellow flowers makes U. kirkiana a popular ornamental tree.Vernonia amygdalina
Ornamental: The tree seems to have good prospects as an ornamental.Vitex keniensis
Ornamental:  Some forms are ornamental.Vitex pubescens
Ornamental: V. trifolia are widely cultivated as ornamentals.Warburgia salutaris
Ornamental: W. ugandensis is often planted for amenity purposes.Ximenia americana
Ornamental: X. caffra is used as ornamental and live fenceXylopia aethiopica

boundary_barrier_support.snippet: Wood is used for fence posts in Australia.Acacia catechu
Trees are suitable as supports for passion fruit and yams.Acacia elatior
Wood of A. laeta is used to make fence posts. The tree can tolerate repeated browsing giving it a good potential as a hedging tree.Acacia lahai
This subspecies makes an ideal windbreak surrounding fields; its narrow crown shades less than other windbreak species.Acacia pennatula
Cut branches are useful for fencing in cattle because of their spines.Acacia seyal
The branches make good fences.Acacia tortilis
Trees are planted as live fences.Afzelia africana

Boundary or barrier:  Tropical cyclones occur at periodic intervals in all parts of its range.  Pacific kauri has an ability to withstand strong winds thereby acting as a wind break or barrier. In certain situations it is suited as boundary marker, due toAilanthus excelsa
Poles and posts from A. anthelmintica are used for fencing.Albizia gummifera
The branches (twigs) are used by tea planters as stakes for laying out tea gardens. These are found to split well. The species is popular along field borders.Albizia zygia

:  An excellent windbreak or hedge for maritime areas, it grows quite quickly and establishes well even in very windy sites. This is an excellent pioneer species for re-establishing woodlands on disused farmland, difficult sAlnus japonica

Boundary or barrier:  The species is known to be used for living fences.   It has good resistance to cyclones and would be well suited for inclusion as an upper-mid-level layer of mixed-species windbreaks of wide dimensions (e.g., greater than 50 m acrossAnogeissus latifolia
Argan brushwood is used for fencing and windbreaks.Artocarpus altilis
The trunk is occasionally used as living support for pepper.Asimina triloba
As a thorny tree, B. aegyptiaca is useful for fencing. Boundary and amenity plantings are widespread in Africa. Cut branches are used to make livestock enclosures.Barringtonia procera
B. rufescens provides a good, impenetrable, browse-resistant live fence; useful for protecting gardens, fields and compounds.Bauhinia tomentosa
In Costa Rica and Nicaragua the establishment of living fencerows from vegetative propagated stakes is common practice, with spacings ranging from 2-5 m.Bombax costatum

In some areas of the Sudan, the tree is being cut increasingly for dead hedging. It is however unsuitable for this purpose and live hedging using other species should be encouraged.Brachylaena huillensis
Used as living fence to delimit pastures, with stakes 1-3 m long and 10-15 cm thick, and spaced 3 m apart or more.Cadaba farinosa
The tree is planted as a hedge and boundary marker in villages.Caesalpinia spinosa
In Southeast Asia, C. cajan is grown as a support for vanilla.Calliandra calothyrsus
Its remarkable resistance to strong winds makes it a good living windbreak for other crops such as bananas and papayas.Capparis decidua
Trees are grown as a live fence.Carissa congesta
The abundant branching habit and the presence of spines make the plant suitable for planting as a protective hedge.Cassia grandis
Wood used as fencing material.Casuarina equisetifolia
In Kenya, farmers plant the tree around fields as a live fence.Casuarina oligodon
In Java, the tree is grown as a boundary tree and fences along roadsides.Celtis australis
Tagasaste forms dense hedges if planted closely.Combretum collinum
C. africana is particularly suitable for planting for live fences and hedges.Commiphora wightii
C. dichotoma is a quick-growing fruit tree, performing well under semi-arid conditions and suitable for planting along boundary and farm roads.Croton megalocarpus
Poles used in fence construction.Cryptomeria japonica
It is grown as a live fence.Dactyladenia barteri
Poles from D. elata are used for fencing.Delonix regia

Thorn branch enclosures prevent livestock from straying at night and protect vegetable gardens, cash crops and fodder- or thatch-grass reserves from livestock. Since it is difficult to control, having an aggressive weedy cDiospyros kaki
D. angustifolia is a good hedge plant for dry areas, useful in sand or marshy soils. The poles are useful in fencing.Dovyalis caffra
In the Kilimanjaro region of East Africa, the tree is commonly grown on the borders of home compounds.Erythrina abyssinica
It is planted as live posts, fence and live supports for yams (Dioscorea alata) and chayote (Sechium edule).Erythrina caffra
Live fence posts are established from stakes as support for vine crops.Erythrina fusca

In India, it is planted as a live hedge around cultivated gardens. When the cuttings are stuck on the ground, they root quickly to give live hedges. It has been used India as support for pepper and grape vines, by virtue ofErythrina sandwicensis

In India, Malaysia and Indonesia E. variegata  is used as live support for betel (Piper betle L.), black pepper (Piper nigrum L.), vanilla (Vanilla planifolia H.C. Andrews) and yam (Dioscorea spp.) vines.  A columnar cultivEucalyptus globulus ssp. globulus
E. tirucalli is an extensively used hedge plant in rural areas of East Africa.Fagraea racemosa
Branches lopped for fencing compounds and livestock enclosures.Faurea saligna
When planted close together, the shrubs make a nice hedge, screen, or windbreak.Feronia limonia
When closely planted, it forms a close impenetrable barrier that serves as a hedge; it tolerates frequent trimming.Flemingia macrophylla
The European ash is commonly used for fence construction.Garcinia gummi-gutta
In Trinidad, the tree is occasionally planted as a live-hedge in grazing areas.Gliricidia sepium
The tree is often planted in hedges and field boundaries.Grewia tenax
In India and South-East Asia, logwood is occasionally cultivated as hedge plant.Hippophae rhamnoides
U’ula is such a reputed fence post provider that it was recommended in the early 1970’s by the Livestock Department, Solomon Islands for a fencing programme.Jatropha curcas
J. procera can be planted on boundaries and as a windbreak.Lagerstroemia speciosa
In the Philippines they are frequently planted around the edges of coconut plantations.Leucaena collinsii
The tree is planted at field boundaries or as living fences.Leucaena leucocephala
L. pallida is largely cultivated on terrace margins or field boundaries.Leucaena trichandra
Dry wood from macaranga have been used for fencing.Madhuca latifolia
The plants are suitable for hedges.Mammea americana
In some areas the species is used as a hedge especially in areas of low rainfall.Markhamia lutea
The termite resistant poles are good for fencing.Mimosa scabrella

Planted as a hedge in courtyards, M. oleifera provides wind protection, shade and support for climbing garden plants. Widely used for live fences and hedges in Kenya, Nigeria, Tanzania, India, and elsewhere. Stakes root easMoringa stenopetala
When spaced correctly, the species can be planted as a live fence.Musanga cecropioides
Poles are used for fencing.Nuxia congesta
O. gratissimum is also cultivated as a hedge plant.Olneya tesota

The thorny varieties of O. ficus-indica such as forma amyclaea and forma elongata are often used as defensive hedges for the protection of gardens, orchards and olive groves through out North America and in parts of ItalyOsyris compressa
Its browse resistance and stout thorns make it valuable as a live fence for protecting arable fields in arid and semi-arid areas.Peltophorum pterocarpum
It is used as a live firebreak in the lower CongoPhoenix dactylifera
Used as a hedge plant in the Philippines.Piliostigma thonningii

With regular trimming, P. dulce makes a dense, almost impenetrable thorny hedge that keeps out livestock and forms useful shelter belts; for hedges, seeds may be sown in 2 rows of 15 x 30 cm.Platycladus orientalis

Trees planted in and around the edges of fields are regularly ploughed and planted with agricultural crops and hence develop vigorous roots, attain great height and diameter, and produce a high quantity of timber.Populus euphratica

P. chilensis could possibly be used to an advantage as barrier plant to form stock-proof hedgerow. If selectively coppiced on a cutting rotation of five years, such hedgerows would, by way of bonus, also provide a perenniaProsopis glandulosa
P. guajava has been used to stake yams (Dioscorea spp.); the small tree is cut back and used to support them. Yield increases of 33-85% have been recorded in Nigeria.Pterocarpus erinaceus
Poles from A. santalinoides are used for fencing.Punica granatum
It is suitable for live fences. The pliable branches are used to support bird traps.Rhamnus prinoides
Wood from R. natalensis is used in making fence poles.Robinia pseudoacacia
Can serve as a live fence.Salvadora oleoides
Poles from the tree are used for fencing.Santalum album
Boundary or barrier:  Sandalwoods are suitable for inclusion in windbreaks, especially where the main windbreak species include good hosts, e.g., Casuarina sppSarcocephalus latifolius
It is sometimes planted as a live fence.Schinus terebinthifolius
Truncheon-cuttings used for fencing around homes in southern Angola.  In some places the tree is highly held culturally and venerable.Sclerocarya birrea ssp. caffra
Has potential use in provision of fencing posts and a boundary tree.Senna siamea
In Uganda, it is widely cultivated as a boundary marker.Sesbania grandiflora
Suitable for use as live trellises for pepper.Shorea negrosensis
The species, either planted or growing naturally, is frequently used for living fence posts.Spondias mombin
S. cocculoides is planted along boundaries and near home compounds.Strychnos henningsii
It is planted to provide green fire breaks in Guinea in West AfricaSyzygium cordatum
Trees planted close together and topped regularly form a dense hedge.Syzygium jambos
T. indica could be inserted into a live fence.Tarchonanthus camphoratus
Yew is a very useful tree for hedging and topiary as it can be closely trimmed. It tends to become a very large bush without trimming. It is used as a windbreak.Teclea nobilis
Trees can be planted as a live hedge.Tecomaria capensis

Suitable for making hedges along contours, around fields and homegardens, as it is not eaten by domestic animals such as buffaloes and goats. It is commonly used for hedgerows, providing mulch for different upland crops.Tephrosia vogelii
In mangrove areas, T. populnea is often planted to consolidate ridges and bunds in an aquasilvicultural system for prawn production.Tithonia diversifolia
The tree is a suitable boundary species.Vernonia amygdalina
Grown in fields and along boundaries.Vitex negundo

V. trifolia is often used as a hedge plant, altough it may trigger various allergic reactions (sneezing, respiratory problems, dizziness, headache, nausea) to people trimming or pruning such hedges.Warburgia salutaris
Suited to cultivation as a hedge plant.Ziziphus abyssinica
Tree useful as a living fence; its spiny stems and branches deter livestock.Ziziphus mucronata
In India, it is commonly erected as ‘brush-wood barriers’ (micro-windbreaks) together with Crotalaria burhia.Zizyphus spina-christi
